sentences.en: A year and a half ago, my colleagues Jody Cantor and Karen Weiss began examining labor practices at Amazon.
sentences.zh: 一年半前，我的同事乔迪·坎托和卡伦·韦斯开始调查亚马逊的劳工做法。

sentences.en: In the process, they met two Amazon workers at a warehouse in New York,
sentences.zh: 在此过程中，他们在纽约的一个仓库里遇到了两名亚马逊员工，

sentences.en: Chris Smalls and Derek Palmer, who had embarked on an improbable attempt to create the company's first union.
sentences.zh: 克里斯·斯莫尔斯和德里克·帕尔默，他们当时正着手进行一项几乎不可能完成的尝试，旨在建立公司历史上第一个工会。

sentences.en: Last week, they did it.
sentences.zh: 上周，他们成功了。

sentences.en: Today, I spoke with Jody, Chris, and Derek about how, against all odds, that happened.
sentences.zh: 今天，我采访了乔迪、克里斯和德里克，聊聊他们是如何在重重困难下实现这一目标的。

sentences.en: It's Monday, April 11th.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月11日，星期一。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Derek.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是德里克。

sentences.en: This is my colleague, Michael, who's the host of the Deal.
sentences.zh: 这是我的同事迈克尔，他是 Deal 节目的主持人。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm going.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我来了。

sentences.en: I'm really grateful because I know you guys are in the middle of what is perhaps the biggest moment of your lives, that you made time to talk to us.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激，因为我知道你们正处于人生中或许最重大的时刻，却依然抽出时间来和我们交谈。

sentences.en: Oh, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, really.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Is everybody good to go if we start?
sentences.zh: 如果现在开始，大家都准备好了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 准备好了。

sentences.en: We got to keep it clean, too, right?
sentences.zh: 我们说话也得注意分寸，对吧？

sentences.en: I might slip.
sentences.zh: 我可能会说漏嘴。

sentences.en: I think if your emotions take you someplace, you should follow your emotions.
sentences.zh: 我觉得如果情感把你带到了某个地方，你就应该顺从自己的情感。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 那么，

sentences.en: Chris and Derek, I want to start by asking you both about how you came to Amazon and to the
sentences.zh: 克里斯和德里克，我想先问问你们两个，当初是怎么来到亚马逊和

sentences.en: JFK8 warehouse in the first place.
sentences.zh: JFK8仓库的？

sentences.en: What was it that brought you both there?
sentences.zh: 是什么把你们带到那里的？

sentences.en: Well, I was employed for Amazon since 2015.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我从2015年开始就受雇于亚马逊。

sentences.en: I was an entry-level worker, got hired as a picker, warehouse associate, got promoted into process assistant my first year, opened up three facilities for Amazon.
sentences.zh: 我是一名基层员工，被雇为分拣员、仓库助理，第一年就晋升为流程助理，为亚马逊开设了三家设施。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: You know, JFK8 was actually my last facility.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，JFK8实际上是我的最后一家设施。

sentences.en: So, you're kind of a veteran at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以，你现在算是这行的老兵了。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对的，对的。

sentences.en: At this time, I was already, you know, a PA for over four years, trained hundreds of the employees, trained management as well.
sentences.zh: 当时我已经当了四年多的流程助理，培训了数百名员工，同时也培训过管理层。

sentences.en: I was hired within the company.
sentences.zh: 我是公司内部招聘的。

sentences.en: And so, I applied to relocate to JFK8, which it didn't open yet.
sentences.zh: 所以，我申请调到 JFK8，当时它还没开业。

sentences.en: It was still under construction.
sentences.zh: 它还在建设中。

sentences.en: So, that was my plan to get into that building upon launch.
sentences.zh: 所以我的计划就是在该大楼一启动时就进去。

sentences.en: And I knew as a, having seniority, I should be able to pick my shift in the days and times that I was supposed to work, especially opening up a new building.
sentences.zh: 而且我知道，作为一名资深员工，我应该能够挑选自己应该工作的轮班日期和时间，尤其是开设新大楼的时候。

sentences.en: But I didn't get that opportunity.
sentences.zh: 但我没有得到这个机会。

sentences.en: They threw me right onto the worst shift, which is 12 hour RT shift.
sentences.zh: 他们把我直接扔到了最糟糕的轮班，也就是12小时的 RT 轮班。

sentences.en: RT.
sentences.zh: RT。

sentences.en: Which is reduced time.
sentences.zh: 也就是缩短工时制。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: 12 hours Thursday, Friday, Saturday.
sentences.zh: 每周四、周五、周六工作12小时。

sentences.en: They took my whole weekend away.
sentences.zh: 他们夺走了我的整个周末。

sentences.en: And I live in New Jersey and didn't have a vehicle at the time.
sentences.zh: 而且我住在新泽西州，当时没有车。

sentences.en: So, my commute was two and a half hours, three hours each way.
sentences.zh: 所以我的通勤单程就要两个半小时到三个小时。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And then had to work a 12-hour shift.
sentences.zh: 然后还得工作12个小时。

sentences.en: So, that's how I ended up at JFK8.
sentences.zh: 这就是我最终来到 JFK8 的原因。

sentences.en: Derek, what about you?
sentences.zh: 德里克，你呢？

sentences.en: How did you come to JFK8, this warehouse in Staten Island?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么来到史坦顿岛的这个仓库 JFK8 的？

sentences.en: Well, similar to Chris, you know, I started working at a facility, EWR4.
sentences.zh: 嗯，和克里斯类似，我开始是在 EWR4 这个设施工作。

sentences.en: In New Jersey?
sentences.zh: 在新泽西？

sentences.en: In New Jersey, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，在新泽西。

sentences.en: Robinsville, New Jersey.
sentences.zh: 新泽西州罗宾斯维尔。

sentences.en: So, I started in July, 2015.
sentences.zh: 所以我是在2015年7月开始的。

sentences.en: I started off as a counter.
sentences.zh: 我一开始是个盘点员。

sentences.en: So, I would like count the inventory.
sentences.zh: 也就是清点库存。

sentences.en: Can I just ask you, what did Amazon mean to you, to have landed a job back in 2015 at Amazon?
sentences.zh: 请问，2015年能在亚马逊找到工作，对你来说意味着什么？

sentences.en: Oh, I mean, you know, at the time, you know, I was unemployed.
sentences.zh: 哦，我的意思是，你知道的，当时我失业了。

sentences.en: I was doing like a lot of different temp jobs.
sentences.zh: 我做着很多不同的临时工作。

sentences.en: And if it wasn't for my mother, I honestly wouldn't be at Amazon.
sentences.zh: 如果不是我母亲，我老实说不会去亚马逊。

sentences.en: So, my mother told me about Amazon.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈跟我提起了亚马逊。

sentences.en: Same.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: She told me about Amazon.
sentences.zh: 她跟我提到了亚马逊。

sentences.en: So, you know, at the time, I didn't really know too much about it.
sentences.zh: 所以，当时我对它其实了解不多。

sentences.en: I just knew that, you know, a lot of people were getting hired at this Amazon facility.
sentences.zh: 我只知道很多人都在这家亚马逊设施被录用。

sentences.en: And I said, you know what, let me just try it out and see what happens.
sentences.zh: 我说，你知道的，让我去试试看会发生什么。

sentences.en: So, I thought that, you know, Amazon was having workers like best intereSt. I thought they were just like, all right, you work hard, you move up.
sentences.zh: 所以我以为亚马逊会把员工的利益放在第一位。我以为只要你努力工作，就能得到晋升。

sentences.en: So, immediately I, you know, adapted that philosophy and I just worked as hard as I could.
sentences.zh: 所以我立刻接受了这个理念，并尽我所能地努力工作。

sentences.en: You were going to move up.
sentences.zh: 你当时觉得你要高升了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That's the, in my mind, I was like, you know what, I'm going to move up with this company and I'm going to excel because Amazon is such a big name.
sentences.zh: 我心里想的是，你知道吗，我要在这家公司高升，我要脱颖而出，因为亚马逊名气这么大。

sentences.en: So, unfortunately, you know, it didn't go that way.
sentences.zh: 所以，不幸的是，事情并没有那样发展。

sentences.en: But, you know.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的。

sentences.en: What do you mean it didn't go that way?
sentences.zh: 你说的没那样发展是什么意思？

sentences.en: It didn't go that way as far as like me getting promoted.
sentences.zh: 就我获得晋升这方面来说，事情没有那样发展。

sentences.en: Did you have a theory about why?
sentences.zh: 你对原因有什么看法吗？

sentences.en: At the time, I didn't know.
sentences.zh: 当时我并不知道。

sentences.en: I thought that I just had to just keep working hard and that
sentences.zh: 我以为我只需要继续努力工作，

sentences.en: I'll be able to get promoted.
sentences.zh: 我就能获得晋升。

sentences.en: But what they did do is they offered me an ambassador position.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实做的一件事是，他们提供给我一个大使职位。

sentences.en: So, ambassador are basically workers who train other workers.
sentences.zh: 所以大使基本上就是培训其他工人的工人。

sentences.en: So, like all the new employees that get hired, it was my responsibility to train them.
sentences.zh: 因此，所有新雇用的员工，培训他们就是我的责任。

sentences.en: And, Jody, how does all of that fit with your reporting on the company and how Amazon operates?
sentences.zh: 乔迪，这一切与你对该公司及其运营方式的报道是如何契合的？

sentences.en: So, what Chris and Derek are describing is their experience.
sentences.zh: 所以克里斯和德里克所描述的是他们的亲身经历。

sentences.en: Based on our reporting on
sentences.zh: 根据我们对亚马逊的报道，

sentences.en: Amazon, that's actually part of the company's design.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是该公司设计的一部分。

sentences.en: Jeff Bezos intentionally created this system where the lower level warehouse jobs were the lower level warehouse jobs.
sentences.zh: 杰夫·贝佐斯刻意创建了这样一套系统：底层的仓库工作就是底层的仓库工作。

sentences.en: Those were expected to have a tremendous amount of turnover.
sentences.zh: 人们预期这些岗位会有极高的离职率。

sentences.en: And then the management jobs in the warehouse or the corporate jobs in Seattle.
sentences.zh: 而仓库里的管理层工作或西雅图的总部工作则完全不同。

sentences.en: Those were totally separate.
sentences.zh: 那些是完全分开的。

sentences.en: And rather than promote people from the warehouse jobs, those jobs he wanted to hire college graduates for.
sentences.zh: 他不想从仓库岗位中提拔人，而是希望为那些岗位招聘大学毕业生。

sentences.en: So, while Karen Weiss and Grace Ashford and I were looking into this warehouse, JFK8, last year, we also discovered that Amazon has a shocking turnover rate.
sentences.zh: 因此，去年当卡伦·韦斯、格蕾丝·阿什福德和我调查 JFK8 这个仓库时，我们还发现亚马逊的员工流失率高得惊人。

sentences.en: This is even before the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这甚至是在大流行之前的事。

sentences.en: It's 150 percent among warehouse workers.
sentences.zh: 仓库工人的离职率高达百分之一百五十。

sentences.en: That's the equivalent of the warehouse workforce turning over every eight months.
sentences.zh: 这就相当于仓库员工队伍每八个月就完全换过一遍。

sentences.en: That's remarkable.
sentences.zh: 这太惊人了。

sentences.en: So, this experience that Chris and Derek are describing, it's actually not only common, but it's part of Amazon's whole business model.
sentences.zh: 所以克里斯和德里克描述的这种经历，不仅很常见，而且实际上是亚马逊整个商业模式的一部分。

sentences.en: And that business model, from what you're saying, doesn't give people like Chris or Derek much of a shot of moving out of the warehouse.
sentences.zh: 从你的话来看，这种商业模式并没有给像克里斯或德里克这样的人提供太多离开仓库的机会。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: We actually found out that one of the times Derek applied for a promotion, he was one of 382 people to apply for the job.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上发现，德里克有一次申请晋升时，他是382个申请该职位的人之一。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's how many people wanted it.
sentences.zh: 有那么多人想得到它。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And just how little chance he had of getting a promotion.
sentences.zh: 而他获得晋升的机会是多么渺茫。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So, you're both, Chris and Derek, initially enthusiastic about Amazon.
sentences.zh: 所以克里斯和德里克，你们两个最初对亚马逊都充满热情。

sentences.en: You see yourself as succeeding in your work, but you start to question that, it sounds, based on your inability to rise.
sentences.zh: 你们认为自己在工作中取得了成功，但听起来，由于无法获得晋升，你们开始对此产生质疑。

sentences.en: How does that work start to change at this warehouse as the pandemic hits?
sentences.zh: 随着疫情的爆发，这家仓库的工作开始发生怎样的变化？

sentences.en: Well, it was just the fact that we were in the dark.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实就是我们被蒙在鼓里。

sentences.en: We didn't know what the hell we was doing, what was going on with the virus, because we're watching it on the news and the company's doing something else.
sentences.zh: 我们根本不知道自己到底在搞什么鬼，病毒是怎么回事，因为我们在新闻里看，而公司却在做另一套。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So, it was something off in there, something off in the building with managers, with communication.
sentences.zh: 所以里面有些不对劲，大楼里管理层之间、沟通方面有些不对劲。

sentences.en: And I'm like, what the hell is going on here?
sentences.zh: 我就想，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: We're in the break room, sitting shoulder to shoulder.
sentences.zh: 我们在休息室里，肩膀挨着肩膀坐在一起。

sentences.en: Derek tell you, we were sitting there joking.
sentences.zh: 德里克可以告诉你，我们当时坐在那儿开玩笑。

sentences.en: We're all going to die because we're sitting shoulder to shoulder and we're watching CNN and they're telling us we need to be six feet apart with masks.
sentences.zh: 我们都快要死了，因为我们肩膀挨着肩膀坐着，看着 CNN，而他们却告诉我们需要保持六英尺的距离并戴上口罩。

sentences.en: Do you remember this?
sentences.zh: 你还记得这个吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 记得。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: What were you feeling in this moment?
sentences.zh: 你当时是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Same way.
sentences.zh: 一样的感觉。

sentences.en: Like, I was scared.
sentences.zh: 就像我很害怕。

sentences.en: I'm like, the energy in the building was just like, everyone was quiet and no one knew what the next steps were.
sentences.zh: 我觉得大楼里的气氛就是，每个人都很安静，没有人知道下一步该怎么做。

sentences.en: We didn't know what Amazon's plans were.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道亚马逊有什么计划。

sentences.en: So, that was the energy that was going on at that time.
sentences.zh: 这就是当时弥漫的气氛。

sentences.en: And Jodi, what is going on for
sentences.zh: 乔迪，此时亚马逊的情况又是怎样的？

sentences.en: Amazon at this moment?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里有这样一个庞大的仓库。

sentences.en: Well, here you have this massive warehouse.
sentences.zh: 它服务于这个巨大的市场。

sentences.en: It's serving this huge market.
sentences.zh: 它服务于纽约市。

sentences.en: It's serving New York City.
sentences.zh: 就在大流行让一切陷入停摆的时候，亚马逊意识到人们想要并且需要我们的服务。

sentences.en: And right as the pandemic is shutting everything down, Amazon is recognizing people want and need our services.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们看到正是在这种充满极大恐惧和极大不确定性的时期，当每一个能被送回家的美国人都回家时，

sentences.en: And so, what we're seeing is that right in this period of greatest fear and greatest uncertainty, when every American who can get sent home is going home,
sentences.zh: 亚马逊正在想方设法让其员工继续工作以满足这种需求。

sentences.en: Amazon is trying to figure out how to get its staff to work to meet this demand.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 大流行带来的这种历史性需求。

sentences.en: This historic demand of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得这就是他们的时刻。

sentences.en: They feel that this is their moment.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的时刻。

sentences.en: And like Chris and Derek are saying, there's a lot of confusion in the warehouse.
sentences.zh: 就像克里斯和德里克说的那样，仓库里有很多混乱。

sentences.en: Our reporting showed that the information Amazon was providing to workers at this point was pretty spotty.
sentences.zh: 我们的报道显示，亚马逊当时提供给工人的信息非常零散。

sentences.en: And workers in the warehouse really did not have a clear sense of what was going on with COVID cases in their own building.
sentences.zh: 仓库里的工人们确实不清楚自己所在大楼里新冠确诊病例的情况。

sentences.en: Did you try to get
sentences.zh: 你有没有试图去了解

sentences.en: Chris from your bosses about kind of what is the landscape here?
sentences.zh: 克里斯，从你的老板那里了解一下这里的总体情况？

sentences.en: There's a virus.
sentences.zh: 有病毒。

sentences.en: It's making people sick.
sentences.zh: 它正在让人生病。

sentences.en: What's my relationship to work now?
sentences.zh: 我现在和工作是什么关系？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, you know, as a supervisor, you know, I felt it was my responsibility to say something.

sentences.en: I got fired the same day of the walkout.
sentences.zh: 我在罢工当天就被开除了。

sentences.en: They called me over the phone
sentences.zh: 他们通过电话通知我

sentences.en: a few hours after the walkout, around like 435.
sentences.zh: 就在罢工几个小时后，大约4点35分左右。

sentences.en: And what was the rationale for you being fired?
sentences.zh: 你被开除的理由是什么？

sentences.en: What did the company say?
sentences.zh: 公司是怎么说的？

sentences.en: I didn't give them a chance to finish.
sentences.zh: 我没让他们说完。

sentences.en: I didn't even give them really a chance to explain it.
sentences.zh: 我甚至没有真正给他们解释的机会。

sentences.en: Jody, what do we come to learn is behind Amazon's decision to fire Chris?
sentences.zh: 乔迪，我们了解到亚马逊决定解雇克里斯的背后原因是什么？

sentences.en: Because we'll turn out to feel quite fateful.
sentences.zh: 因为这件事后来显得相当具有宿命色彩。

sentences.en: So Amazon's official explanation always has been and is to this day that Chris was violating quarantine.
sentences.zh: 所以亚马逊官方一直到今天的解释都是，克里斯违反了隔离规定。

sentences.en: However, I'm going to read you text messages that were sent between two Amazon HR officials on the same day Chris was fired.
sentences.zh: 然而，我要读给你们听的是，在克里斯被解雇的同一天，两名亚马逊人力资源官员之间发送的短信。

sentences.en: They're saying things like, come on.
sentences.zh: 他们说的话像是在说，拜托。

sentences.en: They were social distancing as requested.
sentences.zh: 他们正按要求保持社交距离。

sentences.en: It was a peaceful proteSt. His right to organize is protected.
sentences.zh: 这是一场和平抗议。他组织抗议的权利受法律保护。

sentences.en: This is going to be perceived as retaliation, not a good look.
sentences.zh: 这会被认为是对报复行为，不好看。

sentences.en: These are HR officials within Amazon expressing some real reservations about Chris being fired.
sentences.zh: 这些是亚马逊内部的人力资源官员，他们对解雇克里斯表达了一些真正的保留意见。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They're saying, this is crazy.
sentences.zh: 他们在说，这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: I don't even know what to say.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道该说什么。

sentences.en: So this is proof that even on that day, there were HR people at Amazon who thought this was a very bad idea.
sentences.zh: 所以这证明了即使在那天，亚马逊内部也有人力资源人员认为这是一个非常糟糕的主意。

sentences.en: So then Amazon's chief counsel sends an email.
sentences.zh: 接着亚马逊的首席法律顾问发了一封电子邮件。

sentences.en: In it, he describes Chris as not smart or articulate.
sentences.zh: 在邮件中，他形容克里斯既不聪明也不口齿伶俐。

sentences.en: He mistakenly sends the email email to like a thousand people at Amazon.
sentences.zh: 他阴差阳错地把这封电子邮件发送给了亚马逊大约一千人。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And what he's recommending in the email is that Chris become the face of all organizing in Amazon.
sentences.zh: 他在邮件中建议的是让克里斯成为亚马逊所有维权组织的发言人。

sentences.en: So I just want to make sure I understand this.
sentences.zh: 所以我只想确保我理解了这一点。

sentences.en: An Amazon executive, a senior executive, is saying in a very dismissive way, Chris, let's make you the face of all unhappy Amazon workers who
sentences.zh: 亚马逊的一位高管，一位高级高管，以一种非常不屑的语气说，克里斯，让我们让你来代表所有对亚马逊不满的工人们，

sentences.en: might want to take their grievances public because in his estimation, that will undermine their efforts.
sentences.zh: 他们可能想把自己的委屈公之于众，因为在他估计，这会破坏他们的努力。

sentences.en: I have to ask how that felt to read that.
sentences.zh: 我不得不问，读到这些作何感想。

sentences.en: I'm just, you know, obviously I have the same nonchalant, cool,
sentences.zh: 我只是，你知道的，显然我还是那种漠不关心、冷酷、

sentences.en: calm, collective attitude.
sentences.zh: 镇定、集体的态度。

sentences.en: But, you know, of course it infuriated me.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，这当然把我惹火了。

sentences.en: You know, I just say, okay, noted, not smart or articulate black men.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我只是说，好吧，记下了，不聪明也不口齿伶俐的黑人男性。

sentences.en: You know, that's the stigma.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就是污名化。

sentences.en: That's how they try to stigmatize us.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们试图给我们贴上的污名标签。

sentences.en: We're not smart enough to be on the same level.
sentences.zh: 我们不够聪明，无法站在同一个水平线上。

sentences.en: Derek, what are you thinking at this point when this email from company leadership goes around about your friend?
sentences.zh: 德里克，当公司高层的这封关于你朋友的电子邮件在四处流传时，你当时在想什么？

sentences.en: I was just appalled at that.
sentences.zh: 我对此感到震惊。

sentences.en: Like, how can you guys sit down in a meeting?
sentences.zh: 就像，你们怎么能坐在会议室里开会？

sentences.en: You know, you guys are making billions of dollars and you worried about Chris and he's only making, what, $25 an hour.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你们赚了数十亿美元，却在操心克里斯，而他每小时只赚25美元左右。

sentences.en: So I just, I knew that they wanted to pretty much silence the whole efforts.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是，我知道他们基本上是想压制所有的抗争努力。

sentences.en: Like, anyone who spoke out, that's how they were going to treat them moving forward, including myself.
sentences.zh: 就像，任何发声的人，他们以后都会这样对待他们，包括我自己。

sentences.en: So because you've held this walkout, you've been fired.
sentences.zh: 所以因为你举行了这场罢工，你被解雇了。

sentences.en: This email has gone out about you that's pretty derogatory.
sentences.zh: 这封关于你的电子邮件流传开来，带有相当贬义的色彩。

sentences.en: What happens next?
sentences.zh: 接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: What do you decide to do?
sentences.zh: 你决定怎么做？

sentences.en: At that moment, that's when we decide to continue to advocate for workers.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，我们决定继续为工人发声。

sentences.en: We founded an organization, the Congress of Essential Workers.
sentences.zh: 我们成立了一个组织，即“基本工人工会”。

sentences.en: The Congress of Essential Workers.
sentences.zh: 基本工人工会。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, um, that was just, you know, at the time I'm getting emails from people from all over the country, Amazon workers, non-Amazon workers that just want to help advocate as well.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，当时，你知道的，我不断收到来自全国各地的人们的电子邮件，有亚马逊员工，也有非亚马逊员工，他们也只是想帮忙发声支持。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: So you being fired has turned you into a kind of magnet for lots of people.
sentences.zh: 所以你被解雇这件事，让你变成了一个吸引很多人的磁铁。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I just say, you know what, we need to, you know, form something that's going to, you know, just bring us in collectively as sort of like a coalition.
sentences.zh: 而我只是说，你知道吗，我们需要，你知道的，建立一些东西，你知道的，能把我们凝聚在一起，形成一种类似于联盟的组织。

sentences.en: And we formed this organization and we traveled the country, starting in New York at Jeff Bezos' mansions and penthouses that we can Google.
sentences.zh: 我们成立了这个组织，并走遍了全国，从纽约杰夫·贝索斯的豪宅和我们能在谷歌上搜到的顶层公寓开始。

sentences.en: We couldn't find all of them, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然我们无法找到所有的宅邸。

sentences.en: We missed a couple.
sentences.zh: 我们漏掉了几个。

sentences.en: We missed the one in Miami, but, um, we started in New York and then, uh, we went to DC.
sentences.zh: 我们漏掉了迈阿密的那处，但是，嗯，我们从纽约开始，然后，嗯，我们去了华盛顿特区。

sentences.en: Then we went to Beverly Hills.
sentences.zh: 然后我们去了比佛利山庄。

sentences.en: Then we went to Seattle.
sentences.zh: 然后我们去了西雅图。

sentences.en: Um, and then we, uh, we, at that time, that's when they started to unionize in Bessemer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后我们，嗯，正是在那个时候，他们在贝瑟默开始筹建工会。

sentences.en: And Jodi, remind us what's happening in Bessemer, Alabama at this moment.
sentences.zh: 乔迪，提醒我们此时阿拉巴马州贝瑟默正在发生什么。

sentences.en: Well, it's an important period to note because it really seemed like Chris and Derek did not have a lot of momentum.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个值得注意的重要时期，因为看起来克里斯和德里克确实没有太多的势头。

sentences.en: They had had this initial burst of publicity around Chris's firing and the walkout, but that had really faded at this point.
sentences.zh: 围绕克里斯被解雇和罢工事件，他们曾有过一波最初的知名度爆发，但到目前为止，这股热度已经大大消退了。

sentences.en: It just feels like the company has the upper hand.
sentences.zh: 感觉公司似乎占据了上风。

sentences.en: The pandemic is progressing.
sentences.zh: 大流行正在蔓延。

sentences.en: Americans are very reliant on Amazon.
sentences.zh: 美国人非常依赖亚马逊。

sentences.en: The company is reporting record gains and it's hiring like crazy.
sentences.zh: 该公司报告了创纪录的盈利，并且正在疯狂招人。

sentences.en: Like in three months, it scoops up 350,000 workers.
sentences.zh: 就像在三个月内，它招揽了35万名工人。

sentences.en: That's equivalent to the population of St. Louis.
sentences.zh: 这相当于圣路易斯市的人口。

sentences.en: There's almost no equivalent for that kind of hiring in American history.
sentences.zh: 在美国历史上，几乎没有哪种招聘规模能与之相比。

sentences.en: They're offering healthcare on day one and really solid wages.
sentences.zh: 他们提供第一天就生效的医疗保健和非常优厚的工资。

sentences.en: So the idea that this small band of workers are really going to be able to significantly challenge the company in the midst of all this, it seems really unlikely.
sentences.zh: 因此，这小群工人真的能在这一切当中对公司发起重大挑战的想法，看起来真的不太可能实现。

sentences.en: But then, like Chris says, comes Bessemer.
sentences.zh: 但正如克里斯所说，贝瑟默出现了。

sentences.en: Right, which is this much more publicized and much more organized nationally-led effort to unionize another Amazon warehouse in Bessemer?
sentences.zh: 没错，这是一场宣传力度更大、组织性更强、由全国领导的在贝瑟默的另一个亚马逊仓库建立工会的努力吗？

sentences.en: Yes, this one has the support of national labor groups and eventually some big-name politicians like Bernie Sanders, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.
sentences.zh: 是的，这一次得到了全国劳工组织的支持，最终还得到了伯尼·桑德斯、亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯等大牌政治家的支持。

sentences.en: And Chris and Derek, what are you thinking as you watch Bessemer start to heat up?
sentences.zh: 克里斯和德里克，当你们看着贝瑟默的事情开始升温时，你们在想什么？

sentences.en: I was like, okay, sure.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，好吧，当然。

sentences.en: I support it 100%.
sentences.zh: 我百分之百支持。

sentences.en: And I supported it so much that we decided to drive
sentences.zh: 我非常支持，以至于我们决定开车

sentences.en: 16 hours down there.
sentences.zh: 南下16个小时。

sentences.en: And trust me, we have no attention on that.
sentences.zh: 相信我，我们在那没有任何企图。

sentences.en: So when I went down there,
sentences.zh: 所以当我到那儿时，

sentences.en: I'm expressing to them, like, I'm here as an actual worker, former worker, trying to make that bridge saying, this is the reason why you need to sign up for the union.
sentences.zh: 我向他们表达，听着，我作为一名真正的工人、前员工来到这里，想要搭起这座桥梁并说，这就是你们需要报名加入工会的原因。

sentences.en: I thought that would be helpful to their efforts.
sentences.zh: 我以为这对他们的努力会有所帮助。

sentences.en: Instead, they said, no, we want to do this the Alabama way.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们说，不，我们要用阿拉巴马的方式来做这件事。

sentences.en: And I said, whatever the hell that means.
sentences.zh: 我说，管他妈的这是什么意思。

sentences.en: What's the Alabama way?
sentences.zh: 什么是阿拉巴马的方式？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: But I know now what it is because they didn't allow us to rally.
sentences.zh: 但我现在知道了，因为他们不允许我们集会。

sentences.en: They barely wanted us to talk to workers.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至不怎么想让我们和工人们说话。

sentences.en: They told us, like, you know, we don't really want you to, you know, talk to the workers because it's going to intimidate them even more because you got fired.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉我们，像，你知道的，我们真的不想让你们，你知道的，和工人们说话，因为这会让他们更加恐慌，因为你被解雇了。

sentences.en: It was frustrating because if you're an organizer, his story's a goldmine if you're talking to workers and convincing them why they need a union.
sentences.zh: 这太令人沮丧了，因为如果你是一个组织者，如果你在跟工人们交谈并说服他们为什么需要工会，他的故事简直是一座金矿。

sentences.en: It makes no sense for you to say that, oh, if you talk to these workers, they're going to be even more scared.
sentences.zh: 你说“哦，如果你跟这些工人说话，他们会吓得更厉害”，这根本说不通。

sentences.en: Your job as an organizer is to lay his story into why it's important to have a union.
sentences.zh: 作为一名组织者，你的工作就是把他的故事融入到为什么拥有工会如此重要之中。

sentences.en: They just didn't want anyone else from, especially from the North, because the South and North, for some reason, don't get along sometimes.
sentences.zh: 他们只是不想让其他人进来，尤其是从北方来的人，因为出于某种原因，南方和北方有时合不来。

sentences.en: So I felt like it was like, oh, you guys from New York, y'all can leave.
sentences.zh: 所以我感觉就像是，哦，你们这些来自纽约的，你们可以走了。

sentences.en: We don't need y'all.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要你们。

sentences.en: So it sounds like you don't think the organizers in Alabama are handling this effort correctly.
sentences.zh: 听起来你认为阿拉巴马州的组织者并没有正确处理这件事。

sentences.en: What do you think that they should have been doing?
sentences.zh: 你觉得他们本该做些什么？

sentences.en: Well, what we were doing, well, we were at the Circle K gas station talking to workers at the
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们当时在做的是，我们在圆形K加油站和

sentences.en: Alabama facility, and we noticed that some of them didn't even know about the election coming up.
sentences.zh: 阿拉巴马工厂的工人们聊天，我们注意到他们当中有些人甚至不知道即将到来的选举。

sentences.en: So if this union is so strong, then how come you have workers who don't even know what's going on?
sentences.zh: 所以如果这个工会这么强大，那为什么你们还会有工人甚至不知道发生了什么？

sentences.en: When this, this, this, the biggest story that's going on in Alabama, you need to talk to these workers.
sentences.zh: 当这个，这个，这个，阿拉巴马州正在发生的最大新闻出现时，你们需要和这些工人谈谈。

sentences.en: They need to understand why it's important that we need a union.
sentences.zh: 他们需要明白为什么我们需要工会是如此重要。

sentences.en: We've had thousands and thousands of workers sign support cards.
sentences.zh: 我们已经有成千上万的工人签署了支持卡。

sentences.en: And so, you know, we, we believe that, that those workers will, will turn out and they'll have their voice.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们，我们相信，那些工人会，会站出来发出他们的声音。

sentences.en: They were so confident that they were going to win.
sentences.zh: 他们对能够获胜信心十足。

sentences.en: And I didn't get that type of vibe.
sentences.zh: 而我没有感受到那种氛围。

sentences.en: Workers were not on board the way the media was portraying it as if this union was doing this amazing campaign.
sentences.zh: 工人们并不像媒体所描绘的那样积极响应，好像这个工会在搞什么了不起的运动一样。

sentences.en: That's not what we saw.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的根本不是那回事。

sentences.en: We saw something totally different.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了完全不同的情况。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the reason this matters, and correct me if I'm wrong, Jody, is like, when it comes to a union vote in a place like Bessemer, every single workers vote counts.
sentences.zh: 而这之所以重要，如果我错了请纠正我，乔迪，那就是，当谈到像贝瑟默这样的地方的工会投票时，每一位工人的选票都至关重要。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对如此。

sentences.en: And they were using a more conventional model.
sentences.zh: 而且他们采用的是一种更传统的模式。

sentences.en: This was a big union, the retail workers union.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很大的工会，即零售业工会。

sentences.en: But I think that part of the question in retrospect about Bessemer is how much of this was coming from the Amazon workers inside the warehouse.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，回想起贝瑟麦的事件，其中部分问题在于，有多少阻力是来自仓库内部的亚马逊员工。

sentences.en: Some of it was, absolutely, but not all of it.
sentences.zh: 有些是，完全是，但并非全部。

sentences.en: So the vote is over and it was fairly one-sided.
sentences.zh: 所以投票已经结束，而且结果相当一边倒。

sentences.en: I'll give you the final numbers.
sentences.zh: 我把最终的数据告诉大家。

sentences.en: 1,798 votes against the union, 738 votes for the union.
sentences.zh: 1798票反对工会，738票支持工会。

sentences.en: It sounds like Chris and Derek, Jody, you're all saying a version of the same thing.
sentences.zh: 听起来克里斯、德里克和乔迪，你们说的其实都是同一个意思。

sentences.en: Chris and Derek, what you saw was organizers not really connecting with workers, organizers from a big national union, and that they were taking a top-down approach.
sentences.zh: 克里斯和德里克，你们看到的是组织者并没有真正与工人建立联系，这些组织者来自一个全国性的大工会，而且他们采取的是自上而下的方法。

sentences.en: And Jody, you're saying that's a pretty conventional, traditional, old-school approach.
sentences.zh: 而乔迪，你的意思是这是一种非常常规、传统、老派的做法。

sentences.en: And put it all together, it just didn't succeed.
sentences.zh: 把这些综合起来看，它就是没有成功。

sentences.en: Well, I should say, technically, the fight in Bessemer has stretched on a long time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我应该说，严格来讲，贝瑟麦的抗争已经持续了很长时间。

sentences.en: But the initial vote there to form a union, that did fail.
sentences.zh: 但那里组建工会的初次投票确实失败了。

sentences.en: And when that happened, you know what a lot of people just said was, okay, the conventional wisdom is true.
sentences.zh: 当这种情况发生时，你知道很多人当时的反应就是，好吧，传统观念是对的。

sentences.en: You can't organize an Amazon warehouse.
sentences.zh: 你根本无法在一个亚马逊仓库里组织工会。

sentences.en: So the public takeaway from Bessemer not working, Jody, is that Amazon is kind of ununionizable.
sentences.zh: 所以公众对贝瑟麦失败的普遍看法，乔迪，就是亚马逊基本上是无法被联合起来的。

sentences.en: Is that the vibe?
sentences.zh: 这就是那种氛围吗？

sentences.en: That is the vibe.
sentences.zh: 这就是那种氛围。

sentences.en: It's been a topic of conversation in union circles for so long.
sentences.zh: 这在工会圈子里一直是讨论的话题，已经很久了。

sentences.en: They know that this is the big one.
sentences.zh: 他们知道这是一个极其重要的案例。

sentences.en: This is the second largest employer in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这是美国第二大雇主。

sentences.en: It's on trajectory to become the first largeSt. This is like the defining employer of our time, as my partner Karen Weiss, our colleague, often says.
sentences.zh: 它正朝着成为第一大雇主的方向发展。正如我的搭档卡伦·韦斯，我们的同事，经常说的那样，这是我们这个时代最具代表性的雇主。

sentences.en: And it just feels from the union side like they cannot make inroads on

sentences.en: And night shift was lovely.
sentences.zh: 而夜班简直太棒了。

sentences.en: We had nights on lock from the moment we started.
sentences.zh: 从我们开始的那一刻起，我们就把夜班稳稳拿下了。

sentences.en: You know, people love the fact that we was out there, you know, setting up bonfires.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，大家都很喜欢我们一直在外面生篝火的做法。

sentences.zh: 篝火？

sentences.zh: 我们当时在烤棉花糖吃。

sentences.en: We were singing, you know, guitar, acoustic music and playing music.
sentences.zh: 我们当时在唱歌、弹吉他、玩原声音乐，还有放音乐。

sentences.en: And it just felt like we built a little community right there, right at the bus stop.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像我们在公交车站那里建立了一个小社区。

sentences.en: It basically, we'd be there in the middle of the night, two, three in the morning and workers would just come that were leaving and just sit down, didn't know us.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我们会在半夜两三点待在那里，刚下班的工人会直接走过来坐下，虽然他们根本不认识我们。

sentences.en: And they would sit down and they would tell us honestly, like really powerful stories.
sentences.zh: 但他们会坐下来，坦诚地跟我们分享一些非常震撼的故事。

sentences.en: Sometimes we'd be out there praying, holding hands, crying, singing.
sentences.zh: 有时我们会站在那里祈祷、手拉手、哭泣、唱歌。

sentences.en: It was just like a real, you can't explain the emotions that were going on.
sentences.zh: 那种情感真的无法用言语来形容。

sentences.en: It was spiritual.
sentences.zh: 那是一种精神上的洗礼。

sentences.en: And that's when I knew, like, this is going to work.
sentences.zh: 就在那时我明白了，这一定会成功的。

sentences.en: Like, we were like a glimmer of hope for these workers because when they got off the bus, if we wasn't there, they were like, yo, where was y'all?
sentences.zh: 我们就像是这些工人的希望之光，因为当他们下车时，如果我们不在，他们就会问：哟，你们去哪儿了？

sentences.en: So like, I knew once we got to that point, I'm like, we got some.
sentences.zh: 所以，我深知一旦达到那个阶段，我们就胜券在握了。

sentences.en: And think about it, like, like how we were saying we went to Bessemer and they weren't engaging with the workers.
sentences.zh: 试想一下，正如我们之前所说，我们去了贝瑟默，但他们没有与工人进行互动。

sentences.en: We had to make sure we did that consistently.
sentences.zh: 我们必须确保自己能始终如一地做到这一点。

sentences.en: So this to you is the opposite of the top-down approach you saw in Bessemer.
sentences.zh: 所以对你来说，这与你在贝瑟默看到的自上而下的方法截然相反。

sentences.en: There's people that I know and heard them say, I signed up because I saw y'all out here for the last year.
sentences.zh: 我认识一些人，亲耳听他们说：我之所以签字，是因为过去一年我都看到你们一直在外面。

sentences.en: I respect the hell out of y'all.
sentences.zh: 我对你们佩服得五体投地。

sentences.en: Like, they seen us.
sentences.zh: 因为他们看到了我们的付出。

sentences.zh: 这段时间你们的个人生活发生了什么变化？

sentences.en: We ain't have none.
sentences.zh: 我们根本没有个人生活。

sentences.en: I didn't see my children the last 11 months as much as I saw them maybe three times in the last year.
sentences.zh: 在过去的11个月里，我几乎没怎么见过我的孩子，去年一年大概也就见了三次面。

sentences.en: And the last time was recently, like two weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 最后一次是不久前，大概两周前吧。

sentences.en: So we sacrificed.
sentences.zh: 所以我们做出了牺牲。

sentences.zh: 所以我总是告诉我的团队，只要我们不在那儿，我们就在输。

sentences.zh: 我们当中必须得有一两个人留守。

sentences.zh: 不管你们在做什么，你们都得到场。

sentences.zh: 甚至有那么几次，我们直接通宵睡在那个帐篷里，等着夜班工人下班。

sentences.en: helped, you know, ease the tension.

sentences.zh: 我们在发放衣物。我们在帮工人们……甚至帮大家支付优步车费。

sentences.zh: 他们让他坐公交车回家。

sentences.zh: 这个人要是没能去那家医院，他们直接把他送进去的话……

sentences.zh: 他当时随时可能会晕倒。

sentences.en: But we paid for the Uber, worker needed, ride home.

sentences.en: Here's $10, get on the bus.
sentences.zh: 给你10美元，上公交车吧。

sentences.zh: 为了哪怕争取到一个人，无论付出什么代价，我们都在所不惜。

sentences.zh: 我们最终签署了全国协议。

sentences.zh: 朱迪，你能解释一下那是什么吗？

sentences.zh: 所以现在团队每天都要在休息室里花上好几个小时。

sentences.zh: 就在某一天，克里斯本人来到大楼里给里面的工人们送饭。

sentences.zh: 那天他们叫来警察，以私闯民宅的罪名逮捕了克里斯。

sentences.zh: 他们抓的可不止我一个。

sentences.en: Oh, that was a gem.

sentences.zh: 都看到我每周、每天都在分发物资、食物以及各种东西。

sentences.en: So for them to see me get arrested for giving them food, the people that were undecided or on the fence about the union, they was like full on, we with y'all.
sentences.zh: 所以当他们看到我仅仅因为给他们送饭而被捕时，那些原本对工会犹豫不决或持观望态度的人，立马就变成了坚定的支持者，表态说我们跟你们站在一起。

sentences.en: That was the turning point.
sentences.zh: 那是整个事件的转折点。

sentences.en: They lost the election right there.
sentences.zh: 他们就在那一刻输掉了选举。

sentences.en: That's interesting because it strikes me that's the second time that Amazon's handling of you
sentences.zh: 这很有意思，因为我注意到，这是亚马逊第二次以这种方式处理你，

sentences.en: seems to really play a key role in your understanding of how this all plays out.
sentences.zh: 而这似乎在很大程度上决定了你对整个事件走向的理解。

sentences.en: The first, of course, being their decision to fire you.
sentences.zh: 当然，第一次是他们决定解雇你。

sentences.zh: 这也是我坚守立场的原因。

sentences.zh: 乔迪，在我们聊到那个故事之前，我想问一下，据你了解，这次投票的前景如何？

sentences.zh: 老实说，根据这个故事中大卫与歌利亚般的实力悬殊来看，大家普遍认为这次行动不会成功。

sentences.en: Amazon, we know, spent $4.3 million in a single year on anti-union consultants.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，亚马逊在短短一年内就花掉了430万美元用于反工会顾问的费用。

sentences.en: Chris and Derek, the ALU, had a total budget of $120,000.

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.zh: 而且还有一个事实，那就是在现代，像这样拥有数千名工人的超大型设施要组建工会，基本上是没有先例的。

sentences.zh: 要举一个非常罕见的例子，那已经是十多年前的事了，北卡罗来纳州有一家屠宰场

sentences.en: 15 years to organize.
sentences.zh: 花了15年才完成组织工作。

sentences.en: But if you want to find an example of it happening with a company this big, you'd probably have to go back to the auto workers who unionized General Motors in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想找一个在如此规模的公司成功组建工会的例子，你可能得追溯到20世纪30年代为通用汽车建立工会的汽车工人。

sentences.en: So, over a century ago.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，那是一个多世纪前了。

sentences.en: So, look, it's awkward to say to your faces, Chris and Derek, but the conventional wisdom was that, look, this was a notable effort.
sentences.zh: 所以，听着，当着你们的面说这个有点尴尬，克里斯和德里克，但大家的普遍看法是，这是一次了不起的尝试。

sentences.en: This was a homespun effort.
